newsitem.title: PERU: Shell says to sign Peru gas accord with US firm.
newsitem.headline: Shell says to sign Peru gas accord with US firm.

text.p: Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. said it hoped to sign a letter of intent this month with U.S.-based Transpacific Iron-Carbide Corp for a deal to supply 120 million cubic feet per day of its Camisea gas.
Shell is a unit of the Anglo-Dutch Royal Dutch/Shell group.

The deal would be the largest supply contract the oil giant expected to sign in its project to develop the huge Camisea reserves, Shell's managing director in Peru, Alan Hunt, said in an interview at the weekend.

"We hope to sign the letter of intent saying we will work with due diligence to bring about this huge gas supply that far exceeds what we would supply to anybody else," Hunt said. The supply would be the equivalent of providing energy for a 600 megawatt power station, he added.

The Houston-based Transpacific plans an $800 million investment to construct a plant to produce 3.5 million tonnes of iron-carbide per year at Marcona, 250 miles (400 km) south of Lima on the Pacific coast, according to Peru's government.
Royal Dutch/Shell is mid-way through a two-year license to study the Camisea reserves -- estimated to contain six times the rest of Peru's hydrocarbon reserves.

The operating partner of a joint venture with Mobil, Shell hopes to first produce gas from the fields in 1999 and -- in its full development stage -- bring gas the 300 miles (500 km) west to the coast by 2002.
The letter of intent with Transpacific is part of Shell's efforts to build a market for natural gas in Peru, where industry mainly uses fuel oil and coal as its hydrocarbon energy resources.
